title: Kahana vs OnlyFans: Library Beside Patronage
excerpt: OnlyFans is recurring membership, patronage, or exclusive fan content. Kahana is library discovery and flexible hub pricing beside patronage.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Processed ≈USD 7.2B in payments in 2024, with an estimated USD 5.5B paid out to creators.
Creators keep 80% of subscription and content revenue; OnlyFans takes 20%.
Typical creator earns ≈USD 150–180/month; top 1% generate ≈33% of revenue and top 10% ≈73–75%, highly skewed.

strengths.title: Multiple monetization channels
strengths.detail: Subscriptions, PPV, paid messages, tips, shoutouts, coaching, and livestreaming.

strengths.title: Simple revenue share model
strengths.detail: Clear 80/20 split, creators know they keep most of what fans pay.

strengths.title: Built-in fan messaging and direct relationships
strengths.detail: DMs, paywalled messages, and private content create strong fan relationships and upsell paths.

strengths.title: High earning potential for top creators
strengths.detail: Top creators can earn tens of thousands to millions per year.

weaknesses.title: Extreme income inequality
weaknesses.detail: Top 1–10% capture most revenue; average creators often earn relatively little (~USD 150–500/month).

weaknesses.title: Strong adult content association
weaknesses.detail: Reputation is heavily tied to adult content; non-adult creators may struggle with brand perception.

weaknesses.title: Platform dependency and risk
weaknesses.detail: Creators depend on OnlyFans’ policies and moderation; past proposed adult-content bans highlighted sudden-shift risk.

weaknesses.title: Limited broader brand discovery
weaknesses.detail: Not a general-purpose discovery platform, creators still need external channels to drive traffic.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. OnlyFans is recurring membership, patronage, or exclusive fan content. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

OnlyFans is a subscription-based creator platform where fans pay for content, tips, and pay-per-view.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and OnlyFans side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On OnlyFans you can use Memberships as a first-class product job. Fans already live on that membership surface and prefer tiers, posts, or patronage-native extras.

Using Kahana with OnlyFans

You can use both. OnlyFans keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep patronage-native fans on OnlyFans. Dual-list related work on Kahana so people who browse libraries can find it, join a Club, and pay there too without rebuilding your whole fan stack.
